data.narrative:
Sphere Semi is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by serial entrepreneur Steven Glinert and Princeton-trained photonic integrated circuits specialist Mitchell Nahmias. The company has raised $20M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public comparables in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix at the Series A stage.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage multiplier to the $20M raised proxy, implying a $50M valuation. Peer-median anchoring uses three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, yielding a $2.3B median valuation with a range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public comparables cannot be applied; the Semiconductors sector shows a 20.5x median price-to-sales ratio across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD, but Sphere Semi's revenue is not disclosed.

The two applicable methods produce a wide but defensible range: $42.5M (low estimate blending stage-progression conservatism) to $2.7B (high estimate anchored to peer medians). The median implied valuation is $1.2B. Key uncertainties include the early stage of product development, the absence of revenue data, and significant variance within the peer set—SambaNova's $11.0B valuation substantially exceeds Rebellions and d-Matrix. The final valuation will depend heavily on technical differentiation in photonic integration and near-term commercialization progress.
